title: Around six months, breast milk alone no longer covers a baby's energy needs
summary: WHO says complementary foods become necessary around six months, and that starting them much earlier or later may slow growth.
body: The infant and young child feeding fact sheet says that around the age of six months, an infant's need for energy and nutrients starts to exceed what breast milk provides, so additional foods are necessary. It calls those foods complementary. If they are not introduced around six months, or if they are given before that age, the sheet says growth may falter. This is the 4 August 2026 sheet's statement about timing and growth. It is not a list of first foods, and it is not a growth chart for one baby.
